code_title: M.P.T-104 – Physical & Functional Diagnosis in Musculoskeletal Sciences
faculty: Dr. Shreya Swami, Dr. Bhargav Patel PT

cos.text: Elicit and interpret clinical signs and symptoms of diseases commonly seen in Orthopedics, and interpret clinical tests and special investigations commonly used in the diagnosis of these conditions.
Generate a primary diagnosis and a list of differential diagnoses consistent with typical presentations.
Identify normal and pathological anatomy on diagnostic images.
Discuss how the serious and common disorders and the specialized areas of medical practice may impact on Orthopedic Physiotherapy practice.

Demonstrate a broad range of technical skill in diagnosing the Physiotherapy-related Orthopedic conditions (cardiac efficiency tests & spirometry; sports fitness testing; physical disability/gait analysis & diagnosis; coping-strategy assessment, orthotic/prosthetic checkout, and immobilization effects; ICF application in musculoskeletal diagnosis; medical screening for referred pain and red flags).

pos.title: Communication
pos.text: Demonstrate effective communication and interpersonal skills, which are adapted to meet the needs of diverse individuals and groups

pos.title: Diagnosis and plan of care
pos.text: Develop physiotherapy diagnoses and an individualized plan of care for the management and prevention of movement dysfunction

pos.title: Evidence based practice
pos.text: Apply principles of critical thinking and clinical reasoning to evidence-based physiotherapy practice

pos.title: Teaching and learning principles
pos.text: Apply learning and teaching principles in educational, clinical and community settings

pos.title: Team Member
pos.text: Participate as an effective intra- and inter-professional team member

pos.title: Ethical and legal standards
pos.text: Adhere to safe, ethical and legal standards of current practice (as identified by professional organizations, central and state law and accrediting bodies)

pos.title: Professional Responsibility and commitment
pos.text: Develop responsibility and commitment to the profession and society through life-long learning and involvement in activities beyond job responsibilities

copoMap.scale: 3 = High, 2 = Medium, 1 = Low, blank = no correlation

units.title: MCPFD 1.1–1.8
units.topics: MCPFD 1.1–1.8: Clinical decision making; vital signs; investigative and imaging techniques (blood test, ABG, PFT, radiological examination, CT, MRI, ultrasonography, ECG, dope testing); evaluation, assessment and treatment planning strategies; physiotherapy assessment (ROM, tone, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, coordination, sports specific skills, cardiac efficiency, sensory evaluation, functional and fitness evaluation, spasm, trigger and tender points); cognitive, perceptual and vestibular assessment; electro-diagnosis; clinical electrophysiological testing; electrophysiological studies in neuromuscular diseases; evoked potentials.

units.title: MCPFD 2.1–2.6
units.topics: MCPFD 2.1–2.6: Psychological aspects of rehabilitation in disability; developmental screening and motor control; anthropometry and body composition; differential diagnosis in physiotherapy; functional evaluation, scoring methods, reliability and validity; evaluation of aging.

evaluation.description: Written examination on early-course content: MCPFD 1.1 Clinical Decision Making, MCPFD 1.2 Vital Signs and selected MCPFD 1.3 investigative/imaging topics taught before the test.
Written examination on later-course content: selected MCPFD 1.4–1.8 and Part II topics taught before the test, with questions aligned to relevant COs.
Course-wide clinical reasoning tasks such as assessment interpretation, differential-diagnosis case analysis, developmental/functional assessment task, and individualized treatment-planning exercise.

Short quizzes and structured activities including vital-sign interpretation, assessment selection, imaging/electrodiagnostic interpretation, developmental screening, differential diagnosis and integrated case reasoning.
Practical assessment is planned within the course assessment scheme as prescribed; practical activities are embedded in the lesson plan.
Comprehensive written examination covering the complete prescribed MPT104 curriculum, with questions mapped to COs and appropriate cognitive levels.
